title: I KNOW THE LORD HAS GIVEN THIS LAND

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Before the spies lay down for the night, she went up on the roof and said to them, "I know that the Lord has given you this land and that a great fear of you has fallen on us, so that all who live in this country are melting in fear because of you. We have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan, whom you completely destroyed. When we heard of it, our hearts melted in fear and everyone's courage failed because of you, for the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below." — Josh 2:8-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most remarkable confessions of faith in the whole Old Testament — and it comes from a Canaanite woman with no religious background. Rahab had only heard stories: the Red Sea drying up, the defeat of Sihon and Og. Yet from those reports alone, she reached a conclusion the whole city missed. Everyone in Jericho heard the same news; their hearts "melted in fear." But Rahab heard the same news and believed.

That is the difference faith makes. The same facts hardened Jericho into terror and softened Rahab into surrender. What she confessed is staggering: "the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below." She had grasped that Israel's God is not one god among many, but the only true God over everything.

Faith comes by hearing (Rom 10:17), and Rahab is living proof. She did not see the Red Sea part; she simply heard, and she believed what she heard about God's power and Israel's God.

Here is the seed of the Gospel. The Lord of heaven and earth would one day send His Son so that people of every nation — Canaanite, Indian, all of us — could be brought near. Rahab believed the reports and was saved; we believe the good news of Christ and are saved too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. The same news hardened Jericho but softened Rahab — how do you respond when you hear of God's power?
2. Do you truly believe God is Lord "in heaven above and on the earth below" over your circumstances?
3. What have you "heard" about God that you need to actually believe?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are God in heaven above and on the earth below. Give me a heart like Rahab's that hears about You and truly believes. Amen.
